paragraphs: The following assessments concern on-site cleaning by maids and housekeeping cleaners. They do not predict hiring, qualifications, authorization, or contract outcomes.

The core work of maids and housekeeping cleaners is to clean guest rooms and public areas under procedures and keep surroundings tidy: make beds and change linens, replenish towels, toiletries, and guest supplies, clean rooms, corridors, lobbies, bathrooms, elevators, and stairs, sweep, scrub, and wax floors, clean carpets, furniture, and curtains, dust and polish, disinfect equipment using disinfectants or steam, remove waste under procedures, report damage and lost property, and maintain cleaning carts and storage rooms.

H02 is an author-created fictional paper exercise for guest room 501. The v1 standard requires 4 towels / 3 bars of soap; the room currently has 2 towels / 1 bar, and the cart can supply 3 towels / 1 bar. The task appendix records a cracked lamp, fictional lost property bag F1 to be reported, and bottle X with a missing label. The product's properties / use / protection requirements / room release authority are unknown. Do not touch real objects or use or mix chemicals. The assignment is issued at 07:00 and is intended for handover to supervisor Ding at 07:10, with no receipt provided. The 10 minutes do not mean cleaning is complete. Use 60 minutes in 4 × 15 blocks: copy requirements and unknowns, calculate replenishment quantities, write a paper sequence and proposed abnormality reports, and review versions. The sequence lists only checking conditions → proposed cleaning under job procedures → inspection and reporting; it provides no practical chemical handling steps.

H02 reference: under v1, replenish 4−2=2 towels, leaving a book balance of 1 from the cart's 3; replenish 3−1=2 bars of soap, but the cart has 1 and is short by 1. Do not invent full replenishment. Record the cracked lamp and F1 only as proposed handovers to the supervisor. Without receipts, do not invent repairs or lost property collection. Do not use X while its label is missing; confirm the product and procedures with the responsible person. Paper records do not establish that the room is ready for delivery. The four paper outputs are a requirements / unknowns table, replenishment calculations and shortage table, proposed lamp / F1/X report form, and v1/v2 difference record. Comments are optional and do not establish approval. Spend 15 minutes daily for seven days: 1 copy inputs; 2 calculate requirements; 3 list the paper sequence; 4 list unknowns and unresolved status; 5 change only the v2 standard to 6 towels / 4 bars of soap, leaving room and cart stock unchanged, requiring 4 towels / 3 bars with cart shortages of 1 towel / 2 bars; 6 recalculate versions, optionally asking another person to check; 7 reflect on detail checking and truthful retention of unresolved conditions. This does not prove actual cleaning, chemical operation, or room release capability.

This page covers O*NET 37-2012.00 maids and housekeeping cleaners: performing light cleaning in private homes or commercial establishments such as hotels and hospitals to keep surroundings clean and orderly. Work includes making beds, replenishing linens, cleaning rooms and corridors and vacuuming, sweeping and waxing floors, cleaning carpets and furniture, disinfecting equipment, removing waste, reporting damage and lost property, and organizing and delivering guest supplies. Work mainly involves physical on-site cleaning. This page excludes adjacent roles such as cleaning supervisors, laundry and dry-cleaning workers, building cleaners, and hotel front desk staff.

entries: Inputs: guest rooms and public areas requiring cleaning, linens and bedding, guest supplies such as towels and toiletries, cleaners and disinfectants, cleaning tools and equipment such as vacuums, floor scrubbers and polishers, mops and cloths, cleaning carts and storage rooms, cleaning standards, and inspection forms.

Inspectable outputs: rooms and areas cleaned to standard, made beds and fully replenished linens and guest supplies, cleaning and disinfection records, removed waste, damage and lost property reports and handling records, and maintained carts and storage rooms.

Complete workflow: receive assignments and confirm standards → prepare carts and supplies → clean rooms and beds in sequence → clean bathrooms and replenish guest supplies → clean public areas and floors → remove waste and disinfect → inspect, document, and report abnormalities.

paragraphs: Key judgments: whether cleaning sequences and standards are followed, whether linens and guest supplies are replenished, whether chemical use and protection follow procedures, when to report damage or lost property, and how to protect guest privacy and property.

Environment and pace: mainly controlled indoor environments. Most respondents stand, perform repetitive movements, and walk continually, using common protective equipment daily. Schedules are relatively regular but may involve shifts and weekends; room turnover and inspection requirements influence pace.

Research inputs: occupational identity, tasks, work activities, work context, skills and knowledge, interest code, education, and Job Zone for O*NET 37-2012.00. Pay, employment, and industry data on that page cover this occupation. These findings do not establish mainland Chinese qualifications, wages, or employment categories.

Check first: cleaning standards and inspection requirements, linen and guest supply allocations, chemical use and protection procedures, cleaning equipment condition, guest privacy and property protection requirements, and damage and lost property reporting paths.

Work cycle: start by receiving assignments and confirming standards, then prepare carts, clean rooms and beds, clean bathrooms and replenish guest supplies, clean public areas and floors, remove waste and disinfect, and finish by inspecting, documenting, and reporting abnormalities. Do not deliver a room before all safety conditions and standards are confirmed.

Boundaries with adjacent duties: this page covers only maids and housekeeping cleaners. Cleaning supervisors handle scheduling and inspections, laundry and dry-cleaning workers wash linens and clothing, building cleaners handle non-guest-room areas, and hotel front desk staff handle reception and check-in. Cleaning quality and guest property responsibilities must not be treated as interchangeable with those on this page.

Property cleaners outside guest rooms handle routine cleaning of building common areas and facilities. Maids and housekeeping cleaners focus on guest rooms, linens, and guest supplies; cleaning objects and responsibility scopes differ.

Laundry and dry-cleaning workers wash, iron, and organize linens and clothing. Maids and housekeeping cleaners clean on-site in rooms and replenish linens. The roles often collaborate but use different processes and equipment.
Housekeeping and cleaning supervisors schedule, inspect, and train. Maids and housekeeping cleaners perform on-site cleaning and undergo inspections; management responsibilities differ.
Hotel front desk staff handle reception, check-in registration, and guest communication. Maids and housekeeping cleaners clean rooms and areas; direct guest service and cleaning duties differ.

Boundaries for interpreting pay and employment
Fit signals: start with observable work behavior

To assess fit, first consider whether you can remain attentive while standing for long periods and repeating operations, clean and replenish to standard, use cleaning agents and protective equipment correctly, follow guest privacy and property rules, and take responsibility for cleaning quality and safety. Tools such as RIASEC can only suggest hypotheses and cannot replace real task experience.
Positive signals: attentive cleaning to standard, patience with repetitive work, correct protection when using chemicals, and compliance with privacy and property rules.

Reasons for caution: difficulty standing for long periods or repeating movements, reluctance to follow chemical and protection procedures, a tendency to miss details or inspection requirements, or inability to follow guest privacy and property rules.

Trial activity: calculate replenishment / shortages using the H02 paper inputs, list unknown labels, protection, and release authority, and draft lamp / F1 reports. Another person's calculation check is optional; paper work is not cleaning delivery.

The RIASEC interest code is RC, Realistic–Conventional: a preference for hands-on cleaning and orderly completion of work under procedures. These labels describe activity preferences only and cannot determine competence or qualifications.

General personality scales such as the Big Five do not provide job evidence for this occupation and may be used only for self-reflection. Continue checking against real cleaning, linen organization, and inspection experience.
Type tools such as MBTI and the Enneagram cannot determine competence or qualifications and may be used only for self-reflection.

The group's education and training description, ranging from a few days to one year, is occupational group preparation information, not a uniform requirement for this occupation. In its education survey, 45% of respondents selected less than high school and 36% selected high school or equivalent. Check employer postings for specific job thresholds.

Check training records, skill certificates, equipment permissions, and legally required special operation permits separately. Use chemicals and equipment according to actual labels and job procedures; do not operate before verification. A US certification lookup does not establish Chinese permit conditions.
Entry stage: learn cleaning standards and sequences, linen and guest supply replenishment, chemical protection, equipment use, and inspection records under supervision, retaining process records.

You may first submit the four H02 paper outputs to show truthful quantity and unresolved status records. They do not prove real cleaning or room delivery capability, which still requires qualified training and authorized assessment.

Next step: check the target employer's cleaning standards, chemical and safety procedures, inspection requirements, and guest property rules, then validate quality and safety through supervised real room cleaning.

Moving toward greater responsibility: with experience, workers may mentor within an area, inspect quality, and assist scheduling, or move into cleaning supervision, laundry and linen management, or property cleaning.

source_card.note: Check source scope, limitations, and statistical periods separately against original evidence. Source usage notes: O*NET 37-2012.00 Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners (Summary) provides occupational identity, official description, interest code, Job Zone, skills, and knowledge for 37-2012.00. Pay and employment data on that page cover this occupation. O*NET 37-2012.00 Tasks provides tasks including making beds and replenishing linens, cleaning rooms and corridors, removing waste, sweeping and waxing floors, cleaning carpets and furniture, disinfecting, washing windows and walls, and reporting damage and lost property. The task sample does not imply that every job performs all tasks. O*NET 37-2012.00 Work Context describes prolonged standing, repetitive movements, walking, controlled indoor environments, and protective equipment use. US work context does not replace Chinese law or employer procedures. O*NET 37-2012.00 National Wages (BLS OEWS display): US national annual pay for 37-2012.00 in 2025 at the 10th/25th/50th/75th/90th percentiles was 27,640/30,350/35,510/39,590/48,570 dollars, with corresponding hourly pay of 13.29/14.59/17.07/19.03/23.35 dollars. National percentiles are not starting pay or seniority. O*NET 37-2012.00 National Employment Trends: employment was 1,356,800 in 2024; the official 2024–2034 projection is 0%, Little or no change, reaching 1,362,800 in 2034. Annual openings of 193,500 include growth and replacement, not net increases or current recruitment vacancies. Projections do not guarantee hiring. Industries: 37-2012.00 lists Accommodation and Food Services and Other Services as the main industries in 2024. Industry distribution signals employer settings, not projected growth or demand. O*NET 37-2012.00 Education and Job Preparation: Job Zone 1-2 usually requires a high school diploma or equivalent, with on-the-job training from a few days to one year. The education distribution does not establish a mandatory requirement for every employer. National Certifications: 37-2012.00 is the US national certification lookup provided by O*NET. Certification and training do not establish practice authorization or employer hiring requirements. Generative AI and Jobs (ILO Working Paper 140, 2025) assesses occupational exposure to generative AI at the task level. The exposure index does not equal adoption rates, job outcomes, or hiring probabilities. Average Annual Wages of Employees in Urban Units in 2025 provides average annual wages by industry category for urban nonprivate and private units, including accommodation and food services. Industry averages are not occupational medians and exclude individual businesses and freelancers. Enterprise Remuneration Survey Information (2024) from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security is a pay lookup organized by occupation / position. It covers urban enterprises, excluding government agencies and public institutions; this page did not obtain an entry precisely matching this occupation. The FermatMind Task Impact Scale for Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners organizes tasks that tools may assist and human control points for task-level AI and fit discussion. The editorial scale is not evidence of adoption rates, layoffs, regulations, or credentials.
